title: Bassists: Wellman Braud and Billy Taylor
summary: Braud was a New Orleans bass player who did not read; Cootie thought Billy Taylor the best band bassist, who then dropped out of sight.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well, what kind of a bass player was Braud Brough?
Well, he was a -- what would you call it -- he was a New Orleans bass player. Sort of --
Like march?
No. He was -- but I don't think -- Braud Brough didn't read music.
Did he not?
No.
I didn't know that. Is that right.
He had a good ear, though.
Yeah.
A very good ear.
Yeah. He got a good sound, didn't he?
Yeah. He got a good sound.
But he used to slap the bass at times, didn't he?
That was back in them days.
Yeah.
(Laughter)
I mean, in those early records, you know, that carries like anything, you know.
I think Billy Taylor was about the best bass player he ever had.
Do you, really?
Bass player.
You mean better than Oscar Pettiford? Better than --
Yeah.
No kidding. Not better than Jimmy Blanton?
Yeah. Bass player.
You mean he was a band bass player.
Yeah.
A rhythm section man.
Yeah.
Is that right?
[I didn't say about] solos or nothing.
I used to write solos for him.
Yeah.
But bass player, Billy Taylor was the best bass player.
You mean he could establish the beat and hold it and you could hear him.
Yeah.
You could lean on him.
Yeah.
He was under you. Is that right. And Billy Taylor was in the band a long time, wasn't he?
Yeah. Uh-huh. And he was a very fine musician. And he knew his instrument.
Did he?
Yeah.
Well, did Duke -- he never got to play solos, did he? In those days they didn't have any bass solos.
No, they didn't have bass solos.
What happened to Billy? I don't remember.
Well, I don't know. I don't think he and Duke got along too well.
Never? Not from the beginning?
Well, yeah. But Billy was sort of independent.
Yeah.
You know, and Duke -- something about those two didn't hit it off together there.
Yeah.
But he was a wonderful musician and played wonderful.
Well, what -- where -- who did Billy go to? Do you remember? I mean, he just dropped right out of sight, didn't he?
Yeah, he did.
Isn't that a funny thing? That's sad, when a good musician like that --
Yeah. He was a real good musician.
Is he alive? Do you know?
Yeah. I think he lives in Washington, D. C.
